title: Business Policy and Strategy
topics: Nature and scope of business policy

items.q: Which term is described by “the way tasks and authority are divided and linked among the parts of a firm”?
o: Resistance to change
Functional structure
Divisional structure
Organisational structure
items.s: Organisational structure is the way tasks and authority are divided and linked among the parts of a firm.

items.q: The statement “the danger that new sellers will come in and take part of an existing firm's market” describes which of the following?
o: Industry
Barrier to entry
Threat of entry
Bargaining power of buyers
items.s: Threat of entry is the danger that new sellers will come in and take part of an existing firm's market.

items.q: Which term is described by “the checking of work while it is going on so that faults are corrected at once”?
o: Concurrent control
Corrective action
Feedforward control
Strategy audit
items.s: Concurrent control is the checking of work while it is going on so that faults are corrected at once.

items.q: The statement “the checking of inputs and conditions before work begins so that faults are prevented” describes which of the following?
o: Concurrent control
Feedforward control
Strategy audit
Strategic control
items.s: Feedforward control is the checking of inputs and conditions before work begins so that faults are prevented.

items.q: Which of the following best describes SWOT matrix?
o: a grid that sets internal strengths and weaknesses against external opportunities and threats
the checking of inputs and conditions before work begins so that faults are prevented
a broad end that an enterprise sets for itself and works towards over a period of time
the putting into effect of a chosen course through structure, people and systems
items.s: SWOT matrix: a grid that sets internal strengths and weaknesses against external opportunities and threats. The other options describe Feedforward control, Strategy implementation, Organisational goal.

items.q: Core rigidity may be defined as
o: the test that a target be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time bound
a broad end that an enterprise sets for itself and works towards over a period of time
the set of general guidelines that govern an organisation's major decisions and set limits on what it may do
a former strength that has become a handicap because conditions have changed
items.s: Core rigidity: a former strength that has become a handicap because conditions have changed. The other options describe Organisational goal, SMART criterion, Business policy.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Deliberate strategy?
o: the plan an organisation actually intended at the outset and then carried out
the contest for customers waged by cutting what is charged rather than by other means
the joining of two firms that were competitors at the same stage of production
a way of competing by serving a narrow segment of a market particularly well
items.s: Deliberate strategy: the plan an organisation actually intended at the outset and then carried out. The other options describe Focus strategy, Horizontal integration, Price competition.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Feedback control?
o: the cutting back of activities, outlays or markets in order to survive a period of difficulty
an obstacle such as heavy capital need or strong brand loyalty that keeps new sellers out
the checking of results after the event and the use of the findings to adjust later work
a working arrangement in which independent firms cooperate without merging
items.s: Feedback control: the checking of results after the event and the use of the findings to adjust later work. The other options describe Barrier to entry, Retrenchment, Strategic alliance.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Operating decision?
o: the checking of work while it is going on so that faults are corrected at once
a routine choice about the daily use of resources within limits that have already been set
the broad pattern of choices through which an organisation pursues its long-term aims
a way of competing by producing at lower outlay than any rival in the line of trade
items.s: Operating decision: a routine choice about the daily use of resources within limits that have already been set. The other options describe Concurrent control, Strategy, Cost leadership.
items.t: Nature and scope of business policy

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Joint venture.
o: the unwillingness of staff to accept a new way of working
the slow loss of fit between a firm's way of working and its changing surroundings
a project owned and run by two or more independent firms for a shared purpose
a way of competing by producing at lower outlay than any rival in the line of trade
items.s: Joint venture: a project owned and run by two or more independent firms for a shared purpose. The other options describe Resistance to change, Cost leadership, Strategic drift.

items.q: Which term is described by “the grouping of work by specialism such as marketing, finance or production”?
o: Divisional structure
Matrix structure
Change management
Functional structure
items.s: Functional structure is the grouping of work by specialism such as marketing, finance or production.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Concurrent control.
o: the unwillingness of staff to accept a new way of working
the checking of work while it is going on so that faults are corrected at once
a good that can perform the same function for a buyer as another good does
the step taken to bring actual results back towards the intended target
items.s: Concurrent control: the checking of work while it is going on so that faults are corrected at once. The other options describe Resistance to change, Substitute product, Corrective action.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Unrelated diversification?
o: entry by a firm into a line of trade different from the one it already serves
growth into lines of trade having no common skill or market with the existing one
a non-physical asset such as reputation, a patent or the skill of the staff
an obstacle such as heavy capital need or strong brand loyalty that keeps new sellers out
items.s: Unrelated diversification: growth into lines of trade having no common skill or market with the existing one. The other options describe Barrier to entry, Diversification, Intangible resource.

items.q: Which term is described by “the standards used to rank competing options before one of them is adopted”?
o: Decision criteria
TOWS matrix
Risk assessment
Strategic choice
items.s: Decision criteria is the standards used to rank competing options before one of them is adopted.

items.q: Decision criteria may be defined as
o: the standards used to rank competing options before one of them is adopted
a method of rating how strong rivalry is in a line of trade by examining the pressures that bear on it
a skill or set of skills that a firm performs better than its competitors do
the systematic gathering of information about outside conditions that may affect a firm
items.s: Decision criteria: the standards used to rank competing options before one of them is adopted. The other options describe Distinctive capability, Five forces framework, Environmental scanning.

items.q: The statement “the slow loss of fit between a firm's way of working and its changing surroundings” describes which of the following?
o: Contingency plan
Strategic drift
Scenario planning
Decision criteria
items.s: Strategic drift is the slow loss of fit between a firm's way of working and its changing surroundings.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Resistance to change?
o: the unwillingness of staff to accept a new way of working
a firm that enters a market before its rivals and may thereby gain an advantage
the extent to which customers can force down charges or demand better terms
the grouping of work by product, region or type of customer served
items.s: Resistance to change: the unwillingness of staff to accept a new way of working. The other options describe Bargaining power of buyers, First mover, Divisional structure.

items.q: Core competence may be defined as
o: an edge over rivals that cannot easily be copied or bought away
the danger that new sellers will come in and take part of an existing firm's market
a project owned and run by two or more independent firms for a shared purpose
a bundle of skills that a firm performs particularly well and that others find hard to imitate
items.s: Core competence: a bundle of skills that a firm performs particularly well and that others find hard to imitate. The other options describe Sustainable advantage, Threat of entry, Joint venture.

items.q: Strategy may be defined as
o: the practice of attending only to results that depart widely from the plan
the broad pattern of choices through which an organisation pursues its long-term aims
the slow loss of fit between a firm's way of working and its changing surroundings
a physical or financial asset such as plant, cash or land that a firm controls
items.s: Strategy: the broad pattern of choices through which an organisation pursues its long-term aims. The other options describe Management by exception, Strategic drift, Tangible resource.

items.q: The statement “the gain that arises when two parts working together produce more than they could apart” describes which of the following?
o: Value added
Tangible resource
Core rigidity
Synergy
items.s: Synergy is the gain that arises when two parts working together produce more than they could apart.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Organisational goal?
o: a choice about the long-term direction of the whole enterprise rather than a routine operating matter
the act of selecting one course of action from the competing options open to a firm
a broad end that an enterprise sets for itself and works towards over a period of time
a grid that sets internal strengths and weaknesses against external opportunities and threats
items.s: Organisational goal: a broad end that an enterprise sets for itself and works towards over a period of time. The other options describe Strategic decision, Strategic choice, SWOT matrix.

items.q: Cost leadership may be defined as
o: a way of competing by producing at lower outlay than any rival in the line of trade
the preparation of several plausible pictures of the future in order to test a course of action
a non-physical asset such as reputation, a patent or the skill of the staff
the danger that new sellers will come in and take part of an existing firm's market
items.s: Cost leadership: a way of competing by producing at lower outlay than any rival in the line of trade. The other options describe Scenario planning, Intangible resource, Threat of entry.

items.q: Which term is described by “an edge over rivals that cannot easily be copied or bought away”?
o: Deliberate strategy
Sustainable advantage
Strategic business unit
Strategic management
items.s: Sustainable advantage is an edge over rivals that cannot easily be copied or bought away.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Functional structure?
o: the aim of earning the largest surplus of receipts over outlay that a firm can achieve
the grouping of work by specialism such as marketing, finance or production
a project owned and run by two or more independent firms for a shared purpose
growth into lines of trade having no common skill or market with the existing one
items.s: Functional structure: the grouping of work by specialism such as marketing, finance or production. The other options describe Unrelated diversification, Joint venture, Profit maximisation.

items.q: Which term is described by “an arrangement in which staff answer both to a function head and to a project head”?
o: Functional structure
Matrix structure
Resistance to change
Change management
items.s: Matrix structure is an arrangement in which staff answer both to a function head and to a project head.

items.q: The statement “the shortfall between what was targeted and what was actually achieved” describes which of the following?
o: Feedback control
Management by exception
Performance gap
Corrective action
items.s: Performance gap is the shortfall between what was targeted and what was actually achieved.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Contingency plan.
o: a grid that pairs outside opportunities and threats with inside strengths and weaknesses to suggest actions
a good that can perform the same function for a buyer as another good does
a prepared alternative course to be followed if the expected conditions fail to appear
the step taken to bring actual results back towards the intended target
items.s: Contingency plan: a prepared alternative course to be followed if the expected conditions fail to appear. The other options describe TOWS matrix, Substitute product, Corrective action.

items.q: The statement “the cutting back of activities, outlays or markets in order to survive a period of difficulty” describes which of the following?
o: First mover
Cost leadership
Price competition
Retrenchment
items.s: Retrenchment is the cutting back of activities, outlays or markets in order to survive a period of difficulty.

o: a review of what an organisation owns and can call upon in pursuing its aims
the grouping of work by product, region or type of customer served
the sequence of introduction, growth, maturity and decline through which a line of trade passes
a declaration of the purpose of an organisation and of the customers it exists to serve

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Strategic drift.

the contest for buyers waged through quality, design, service and promotion rather than through charges
the slow loss of fit between a firm's way of working and its changing surroundings

items.q: The statement “a measure chosen to show whether an important aim is being met” describes which of the following?

Key performance indicator
Objective
Profit maximisation

o: a former strength that has become a handicap because conditions have changed
a grid that sets internal strengths and weaknesses against external opportunities and threats
a choice about the long-term direction of the whole enterprise rather than a routine operating matter
a measure chosen to show whether an important aim is being met

a bundle of skills that a firm performs particularly well and that others find hard to imitate

o: an obstacle such as heavy capital need or strong brand loyalty that keeps new sellers out
the arrangement of aims from broad purposes at the top down to narrow targets at the base

a grid that pairs outside opportunities and threats with inside strengths and weaknesses to suggest actions

items.q: All of the following belong to Strategy implementation EXCEPT
o: Performance gap
Functional structure
Organisational structure
Strategy implementation
items.s: Every other option belongs to Strategy implementation. “Performance gap” belongs to Strategy evaluation and control, not Strategy implementation.

a former strength that has become a handicap because conditions have changed

the practice of measuring one's own results against those of the best performer available
entry by a firm into a line of trade different from the one it already serves

Tangible resource
Intangible resource

items.q: The statement “the difference between what a firm receives for its output and the outlay on what it bought in” describes which of the following?

Tangible resource
Value added
Benchmarking
items.s: Value added is the difference between what a firm receives for its output and the outlay on what it bought in.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Board of directors?
o: the body elected by the owners of a company to watch over its affairs on their behalf
a routine choice about the daily use of resources within limits that have already been set
a choice about the long-term direction of the whole enterprise rather than a routine operating matter
the way tasks and authority are divided and linked among the parts of a firm

Conglomerate merger
Vertical integration

a good that can perform the same function for a buyer as another good does
a way of competing by producing at lower outlay than any rival in the line of trade

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines TOWS matrix.

any individual or group that can affect, or is affected by, the achievement of an organisation's aims

the set of general guidelines that govern an organisation's major decisions and set limits on what it may do
a former strength that has become a handicap because conditions have changed

o: the broad pattern of choices through which an organisation pursues its long-term aims
a pattern of action that grows from daily choices rather than from a written plan
the ambitious long-term aim an organisation sets for itself even when its present means are modest
an edge over rivals that cannot easily be copied or bought away
items.s: Emergent strategy: a pattern of action that grows from daily choices rather than from a written plan. The other options describe Sustainable advantage, Strategy, Strategic intent.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Profit maximisation.
o: a specific and measurable target to be reached within a stated period
the aim of earning the largest surplus of receipts over outlay that a firm can achieve
a broad end that an enterprise sets for itself and works towards over a period of time
a measure chosen to show whether an important aim is being met
items.s: Profit maximisation: the aim of earning the largest surplus of receipts over outlay that a firm can achieve. The other options describe Organisational goal, Key performance indicator, Objective.

items.q: Three of these relate to Environmental and industry analysis. Which one does not?
o: Environmental scanning
Industry
Organisational structure
PESTLE analysis
items.s: Every other option belongs to Environmental and industry analysis. “Organisational structure” belongs to Strategy implementation, not Environmental and industry analysis.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the obligation of an enterprise to consider the welfare of the wider society in the conduct of its affairs”
o: Strategic decision
Corporate social responsibility
Operating decision
Corporate governance
items.s: Corporate social responsibility is the obligation of an enterprise to consider the welfare of the wider society in the conduct of its affairs.
items.t: Nature and scope of business policy

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Corporate governance?
o: a person who holds part ownership of a company through the units of stock they have bought
any individual or group that can affect, or is affected by, the achievement of an organisation's aims
the set of general guidelines that govern an organisation's major decisions and set limits on what it may do
the system by which the owners of an enterprise oversee and hold to account those who run it
items.s: Corporate governance: the system by which the owners of an enterprise oversee and hold to account those who run it. The other options describe Business policy, Stakeholder, Shareholder.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Management by exception?
o: the practice of attending only to results that depart widely from the plan
the checking of results after the event and the use of the findings to adjust later work
the shortfall between what was targeted and what was actually achieved
a periodic review of whether a firm's chosen course still fits its surroundings
items.s: Management by exception: the practice of attending only to results that depart widely from the plan. The other options describe Performance gap, Feedback control, Strategy audit.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Vertical integration.
o: entry by a firm into a line of trade different from the one it already serves
the joining of firms at different stages of the same production chain
the union of firms in unrelated lines of trade under one ownership
growth into a neighbouring line of trade that shares skills or channels with the present one
items.s: Vertical integration: the joining of firms at different stages of the same production chain. The other options describe Diversification, Related diversification, Conglomerate merger.
